body.statement:
Every intensity-optimized clipped-ramp member lies in Li and Zhao's baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class and fails the negligible-increment requirement used for their Gaussian AIPW conclusion. Therefore every sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets that is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over that baseline class inherits, for every \(0<d<d_{\max}\) and each sign of the corresponding intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\geq d\}
 \geq[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha]_+,
\]
where \(d_{\max}\), \(x(d)\), and \(H\) are those of the jointly optimized frontier theorem. Only this converse transfers by subclass inclusion. Neither the pair-specific attaining rule nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem is asserted on Li and Zhao's larger class.
body.proof_tex:
The sourced baseline-class node states the relevant published requirements. In the present construction,
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,\bar q_\star(t/n)/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
Both probabilities are deterministic functions of every available history, strictly positive, strictly below one, and sum to one. The membership proposition proves that the potential outcomes are fixed and bounded and that the zero regression is predictable. Thus every member belongs to Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.

We verify the Gaussian obstruction directly. Write
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\},
 \qquad
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
The martingale increments are orthogonal by iterated conditioning. Therefore the variance of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error is
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^ng(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive at every \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\), while \(g(t/n)=0\) at all earlier indices. Hence
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n
 \frac{(t/n)g(t/n)^2}{\bar q_\star(t/n)}
 -\frac1{n^2}\sum_{t=1}^ng(t/n)^2
 \longrightarrow
 w_\star:=\int_{a_\star}^1
 \frac{u g(u)^2}{\bar q_\star(u)}\,du>0.
\]
The limit is finite because \(\bar q_\star\geq c/2\), and it is strictly positive because \(M,L_r>0\) and \(a_\star<1\).

At the unprojected two-arm-vector level, the control potential outcome and its regression are identically zero, so the AIPW covariance has a zero control row and column. Its smallest eigenvalue is zero, and the displayed Condition 3(ii) premise cannot hold. The obstruction is not merely this singular coordinate: it persists after projection to the nondegenerate treated contrast. Indeed, let \(q_1=\bar q_\star(1)\in[c/2,c]\) and \(g_1=g(1)>0\). At \(t=n\), for all sufficiently large \(n\), the smallest binary assignment probability is \(q_1/n\), and the source's outcome-plus-regression envelope is at least \(g_1\). The scalar negligible-maximum analogue satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}
 \max_{1\leq t\leq n}
 \frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \geq\frac{g_1^2}{q_1^2w_\star}>0.
\]
It is not \(o(1)\), verifying that the late rare-arm increments remain nonnegligible even in the positive-variance projection.

Uniform honesty on Li and Zhao's baseline class implies honesty on this deterministic-propensity two-sign subclass. Applying the jointly optimized frontier theorem gives the displayed bound. This inclusion argument constructs no confidence procedure on the larger class, so it transfers neither exact attainment nor the positive structured-profile calibration theorem.
body.justification: Subclass inclusion transfers the joint intensity-and-residual converse to procedures claimed uniformly honest over Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.
body.gap: The transfer requires both the sourced class comparison and a direct verification that the intensity-optimized critical arrays retain nonnegligible late increments outside the Gaussian Condition 3(ii) regime.
body.consumer: Readers may use the joint lower envelope against baseline-class honesty claims, but not as a positive or globally attained result on that larger class.
